title: How much of a record-speed Rubik’s Cube solve is the scramble?
verdict_why: Proceed only with the named change to record-like extremes in audited single-group 3x3 finals, requiring at least 500 eligible finals, 20,000 confirmatory attempts and 100 solver-season extremes. Exact world-record attribution additionally requires a verified scramble link for that attempt; otherwise it is an illustrative motivation only. Missing competitor-group assignment invalidates the original all-round claim.

prior_work.citation: Potential development of the 3x3 Rubik’s Cube World Record (single), dataisbeautiful (2023)
prior_work.finding: Fits record progression including a Gompertz model. Calendar record extrapolation is not novel.

novelty_status: survives only with a named change
novelty_why: Change from “was the world record lucky?” to an exposure-adjusted, peer-measured scramble advantage for each solver’s fastest final-round solve of a season, using audited single-group finals. Published reconstructions already answer the generic luck question; the searched academic/popular work did not supply this counterfactual. Five queries used; absence is a bounded search verdict. A specific world record is tested only if it falls in the linked subset.
estimand: For eligible solver-seasons, the geometric-mean ratio of estimated time on a median-difficulty scramble to the observed fastest 333 final-round solve that season, holding solver/date skill fixed. Cohort: the top 100 solvers by 2018 official 333 average ranking with at least 50 pre-2019 valid attempts; solver-seasons must have at least five eligible final rounds. Secondary: frequency of extreme solves beyond a fixed-skill, actual-attempt-exposure null. Inference is for this finals cohort, not all world records.
identification: Crossed model for log valid time with solver-specific time trends, competition-round conditions, attempt-position effects and scramble effects. Peers in an audited single group identify relative scramble advantage within the same round; estimate each extreme’s scramble effect leaving that solver out. Fit a joint DNF component. Learn priors, feature choices and tuning only on pre-2019 eligible finals, freeze the estimation algorithm, then estimate nuisance skill/difficulty with cross-fitting on 2019–2025 and apply the pre-fixed seasonal-minimum selection. Simulate actual finalist lineups, attempt counts and calendar, retaining round/solver dependence and reselecting each seasonal minimum. This is a conditional shared-environment comparison, not a causal partition of innate skill and luck; exact historical world-record examples require independently verified mapping.
strongest_objection: A scramble favours particular solving methods/orientations and interacts with a solver’s skill; a common random effect can mistake a solver-specific opportunity for general luck. Record selection also exaggerates residuals.
fix: Estimate difficulty from other finalists with cross-fitting; fit solver-by-scramble-feature interactions using transparent cross/first-pair features, and bootstrap the entire record-selection procedure. Treat unmeasured execution luck as residual, not scramble causation; restrict claims to the shared component. Reject coverage if group or extra-attempt mapping is ambiguous.
robustness: Compare Gaussian log-time and heavy-tailed models, with and without DNF joint modelling; cluster resampling by competition and solver.
Replicate in 2019–2022 and 2023–2025; require stable sign with leave-one-season, leave-one-solver and alternative pre-fixed best-of-five rather than seasonal-minimum estimates.
Placebo permute attempt-position scramble labels within eligible rounds; compare peer difficulty with solver-computed cross/first-pair features, not God’s-number distance as a sole proxy.
prereg_rule: Primary claim “shared scramble luck materially helps extreme solves” passes if the geometric-mean median-scramble/observed-time ratio across pre-defined solver-season minima exceeds 1.10 and its competition/solver clustered bootstrap 95% lower bound exceeds 1.00 (2,000 resamples, seasonal-minimum selection repeated). Otherwise it does not pass; call inconclusive if the interval spans both 1.00 and 1.10. Coverage gate: >=500 eligible finals, >=20,000 confirmatory attempts, >=100 eligible solver-season extremes. Freeze top-100 cohort from 2018 average ranking and the >=50 pre-2019 attempt requirement; require >=5 eligible finals per solver-season. Do not replace missing finals with an all-round scramble join. Record-arrival null is secondary (10,000 simulations); specific world-record claims require a verified link and are case studies, not this primary estimand.

exploration_slice.definition: Only pre-2019 333 finals with exactly one non-extra scramble group and complete five-attempt mapping; order rounds by SHA256(competition_id|round_type_id), take up to 100 rounds and first 20 competitors per round by hashed person_id. Exclude every selected competition from confirmation. Metadata/header reads so far are not an outcome pilot.
exploration_slice.rows: At most 10,000 attempt rows (100 rounds × 20 competitors × 5); realised count must be recorded at extraction, not yet measured.
exploration_slice.size: <=3 MB projected minimal joined CSV (cap 300 bytes/row); exact emitted bytes to be logged. Streaming ZIP extraction reads a 378.74 MB source later; no full download in verification.

belief: A single world-record solve proves someone is the fastest cuber.
obvious_answer: Rank solvers by their best official time.
flaw: Best-of-many attempts rewards opportunity and easy scrambles; most rounds also use different scramble groups.
fairer_test: Compare the same scramble among audited finalists, infer its shared advantage without the extreme solver, then replay the seasonal-best race with the observed opportunities.
possible_verdicts: Records receive a large shared scramble boost, while exceptional skill remains necessary.
Peer-measured scramble difficulty explains little; solver execution or solver-specific opportunities dominate the extreme result.
central_visual: Each fastest final-round solve of a season moves to its estimated median-scramble time with an uncertainty band, beside the other finalists on the identical scramble and the simulated extreme-time envelope. Add a world-record example only when directly linked.
shorts: One scramble, several finalists: how much do everyone’s times move?
Why five solves and one single record measure different things.
More attempts can break a record even if nobody improves.
companion_assumption: Change the counterfactual scramble percentile from the 50th to the 25th or 75th; refit-free predictions move the adjusted time.

Novelty.why: Shared-scramble and exposure counterfactual is distinct; generic luck story is already covered.

Rigour.why: Peer comparison and selection-aware simulation work on audited finals; method interactions limit attribution.

Data.why: Full population, downloadable and republishable; missing group links restrict usable coverage.

Hook.why: Skill versus luck in a spectacular record is immediate.

Verdict either way.why: Large or small shared luck both revise what a record measures.

Visual.why: One shared-scramble comparison and adjusted-time interval carries the turn.

Feasibility.why: Laptop-sized archive; eligibility audit and record-selection model take roughly eight days.
